causes.cause: `process.kill(-k.pid, "SIGKILL")` sends a negative pid. On win32, libuv's uv_kill calls OpenProcess(-pid), which fails, and Node throws ESRCH. That error is uncaught at top-level await and kills the file in section 6. It masks sections 8-23, the trust-model check and section 21, about 75 checks.
causes.fix: On win32, run spawnSync('taskkill', ['/T','/F','/PID', String(k.pid)]) instead. Keep process.kill(-pid) on POSIX. The /T flag also ends the hung `node -e setTimeout(60000)` grandchild, whose cwd is A.d. Otherwise the fs.rmSync(tmp) at 1049 can hit EBUSY, because Windows cannot delete a process's working folder.

causes.cause: review-round.mjs:161-163 keys the repo as `git:${realpathSync(resolve(tree, common))}`. In a main worktree, git prints a relative `.git`, so the key keeps the cwd's 8.3 spelling (C:\Users\RUNNER~1\...). In a linked worktree, git prints its long final path. pi-review's immutable checkout is always a linked worktree, so its key is always long. One item therefore splits into two scopes, which violates R-705: the round cap resets when you switch launcher or worktree. The tree root is realpathSync of git's long --show-toplevel, while --out keeps the short spelling, so relUnder() returns null. The tracked --out refusal (R-724) and the snapshot exclusion both stop working: a review overwrites tracked file f, and an in-tree --out reads as 'changed during the review'. This log shows the same construct failing: land.test prints 'refused: --tree and --main must share one git repository' 36 times, from nana-land.mjs:71. The failure is masked behind layers 1-3.
causes.fix: Product fix: on win32, use realpathSync.native (like fsReal at pi-worker.mjs:154) for the repo key, for root in treeScope, and for realOut in review-round.mjs. Also use it for the report --repo key at review-ledger.mjs:51. Keep the test's short tmp as the regression evidence. Test-only alternative: fs.realpathSync.native at line 26 should make the file pass. That leaves a Windows residual against R-705 and R-724 for any cwd or --out spelled differently from git's final path, such as 8.3 names or a lowercase drive letter (the key is a case-sensitive string compare).

causes.cause: `"x".repeat(50000)` goes on the command line as --item. Windows CreateProcess caps a command line at 32,767 characters, so spawnSync returns an error with status null. The check '--item "xxxxxxxxxx…" refused, no stack' then fails.
causes.fix: Use a length well over SLUG_MAX (128) that fits the Windows limit, such as "x".repeat(20000), on every platform or only on win32.

Every review there gets a +snap: revision, which contradicts R-708, and nana-land's match by sha may fail on Windows.

causes.cause: On Windows `signaled.kill("SIGTERM")` is TerminateProcess. pi-review's SIGTERM handler never runs, so 'close' gives code null (not 143) and the worktree registration remains. The detached fake pi, which waits on never-release forever, is orphaned with the checkout as its cwd. Today the reclaim bug hides the knock-on effect. Once reclaim is fixed, the next launch's `git worktree remove --force` fails on that busy folder and throws 'cannot reclaim stale review worktree'. Every later pi-review would then refuse, failing checks 11-17.
